After Erling Haaland had an equaliser controversially disallowed, England midfielder Anderson netted with a sweet volley just before the hour to cancel out Rodrigo Muniz's well-crafted opener.

It was enough to end City's run of three successive Premier League defeats but left them without a win in the competition for five weeks after opening the campaign with seven wins in a row.

The main talking point was Haaland's disallowed goal after 25 minutes, when the Norwegian prodded home from close range after a fumble by Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. To City's frustration, the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball.

The draw ended Fulham's run of 20 consecutive defeats against City in all competitions and continued their recent upturn in form under Alvaro Arbeloa, with the Cottagers now unbeaten in five Premier League games.

With Tuesday's clash against Napoli in mind, City boss Enzo Maresca paired Ayyoub Bouaddi with Anderson in midfield, naming Enzo Fernández on the bench after his later return from international duty.

They struggled to assert control against the hard-working visitors, although Haaland threatened early on when he was denied by a good challenge from David Affengruber.

Fulham took the lead with a well-worked goal after 16 minutes, breaking quickly from a throw deep inside their own half.

Josh King released Oscar Bobb down the right and the former City forward cut inside Anderson to find Muniz. The Brazilian wrong-footed Abdukodir Khusanov with a superb first touch and curled a shot into the roof of the net.

Facing another defeat, City needed to respond and controversy erupted after Haaland thought he had equalised.

Phil Foden had spread play wide with Iliman Ndiaye crossing for the prolific Norwegian. Haaland did not make clean contact with his volley, but Leno failed to gather it securely and appeared to drop the ball before the striker poked in at the second attempt.

The goal was chalked off by referee Thomas Bramall and VAR Sam Barrott did not overturn the decision, ruling to Haaland's clear frustration that Leno -- because the ball was between his hands -- had retained control.

That may have still been bothering Haaland when he uncharacteristically blazed over from close range after being teed up by Foden soon after.

Yet City looked lethargic and Fulham seemed the more enterprising team until the hosts clawed their way back into the game with Anderson's sweetly-struck volley.

A corner was cleared only as far as the England midfielder on the edge of the area, and he watched patiently before connecting with a powerful shot that travelled through a crowded area and past an unsighted Leno.

Anderson went close again from a Haaland cutback but Fulham continued to cause problems with Muniz drawing a good save from Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Both sides battled on but neither could fashion a winning opportunity in the closing stages.
